claims.text: The alloy system is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi produced by selective laser melting.
The as-produced alloy is initially single-phase.
Rapid solidification during SLM forms Mn2O3 precipitates.
The as-produced alloy contains approximately 27 nm Mn2O3 precipitates at cell or grain boundaries.
The as-produced SLM CoCrFeMnNi alloy has high strength.
The as-produced alloy has high ductility and toughness without significant brittle failure.
Controlled oxygen enrichment promotes coarsening and possible interconnection of Mn2O3 precipitates.
Post-process thermal aging promotes coarsening and possible interconnection of Mn2O3 precipitates.
Fine Mn2O3 precipitates provide beneficial Zener pinning.
Coarsening of Mn2O3 precipitates reduces their Zener-pinning effect.
Coarsened or interconnected boundary precipitates create local stress concentrations and weaken grain-boundary cohesion.
Stress concentration and weakened boundary cohesion promote localized intergranular fracture and a ductile-to-brittle transition.
The proposed precipitate-mediated mechanism differs from conventional alloys, in which grain-boundary solute segregation predominates.
The cited SLM CoCrFeMnNi alloy was mechanically tested at temperatures from room temperature through 700 °C.
The cited alloy retained superior strength through approximately 700 °C.
The proposed embrittlement mechanism applies under typical service temperatures up to about 700 °C and steady loading rates.
At much higher temperatures or extreme strain rates, other deformation or failure mechanisms may dominate.
Oxygen-enriched or aged specimens will exhibit lower toughness and ductility than the as-produced baseline.
Oxygen-enriched or aged specimens will show more intergranular or brittle fracture features than the as-produced baseline.
No loss of toughness or ductility after confirmed precipitate coarsening would falsify the proposed causal mechanism.

contradictions.description: The alloy is described as single-phase while also being described as containing a distinct Mn2O3 precipitate phase. This is inconsistent unless 'single-phase' is explicitly restricted to the metallic matrix.
